latest_release.name: RubyLLM 2.1.1
latest_release.body:
RubyLLM 2.1.1 fixes fresh installs that today's faraday-net_http 3.5.0 release broke, connects to MCP servers that predate the 2026-07-28 revision, and keeps batch embeddings paired with the right inputs.

```sh
bundle add ruby_llm --version 2.1.1
```

Already on 2.1? Run `bundle update ruby_llm`. No schema or code changes are needed.

## Fixed

- **Install RubyLLM with the latest faraday-net_http.** faraday-net_http 3.5.0 falls outside the range every Faraday from 2.0.1 to 2.14.4 accepts, so a fresh `bundle install` resolved Faraday 2.0.0, which loads no default adapter, and every request failed with `:net_http is not registered on Faraday::Adapter`. RubyLLM now excludes Faraday 2.0.0. By @crmne; thanks @juneira. ([ef2bebdb](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/ef2bebdb))
- **Connect to MCP servers that predate the 2026-07-28 revision.** A server that rejects the revision with `-32022` now gets the `initialize` handshake whether it lists the legacy revisions it speaks, as Atlassian's does, or lists none, as Datadog's does. By @ebeigarts, @juneira, and @crmne. (#1056, #1057, #1053, #1055)
- **Pair batch embeddings with the right inputs.** OpenAI-compatible and Mistral batch results now place each vector by the position the provider reports, and mark a result with duplicate, missing, or out-of-range positions as failed instead of pairing its vectors with the wrong texts. By @D41910. (#1051, #1052)
- **Keep the Bedrock inference profile you choose.** An id that already names a geography, such as `eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, is no longer rewritten to another region's profile, so requests stay where your IAM policy allows them. By @s-andringa. (#1050)
- **Keep chat replies when a usage row cannot be linked.** A persisted chat saves the reply and logs the failed link, instead of rolling back an answer the provider already billed. By @yorzi. (#1048, #1049)
- **Upload converted attachments again after a provider deletes them.** The chat forgets the stale upload and retries, as it already did for plain attachments. By @yorzi. (#1046, #1047)

## Thanks

Thanks to @yorzi, @s-andringa, @D41910, @ebeigarts, and @juneira for the fixes and reports in this release.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/compare/v2.1.0...v2.1.1

detail.readme_excerpt:
The Ruby AI framework

Build AI features the Ruby way: models, tools, agents, evaluations, and Rails conventions, designed together, with one consistent API.

```ruby chat = RubyLLM.chat chat.ask "What's the best way to learn Ruby?" chat.ask "What's in this image?", with: "ruby_conf.jpg" chat.with_model("claude-sonnet-5").ask "Now say it as a haiku" RubyLLM.paint("a sunset over mountains in watercolor").save("sunset.png") ```
[Website](https://rubyllm.com/) · [Getting Started](https://rubyllm.com/getting-started/) · [What's New in 2.1](https://rubyllm.com/whats-new-in-2-1/) Battle tested at [](https://chatwithwork.com) - *Fully private work AI* [![Gem Version](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ruby_llm.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ruby_llm) [![Ruby Style Guide](https://img.shields.io/badge/code_style-rubocop-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop) [![Gem Downloads](https://img.shields.io/gem/dt/ruby_llm)](https://rubygems.org/gems/ruby_llm) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/crmne/ruby_llm/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/crmne/ruby_llm)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/519fcb20-ab8c-4af3-9185-0953b3ba7b81 > [!NOTE] > Using RubyLLM? [Share your story](https://tally.so/r/3Na02p)! Takes 5 minutes. --- ## 23 providers. One API. Build with the models you want. Move between hosted and local providers without rewriting your application, or connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. [Browse models and pricing](https://rubyllm.com/available-models/) · [Connect a provider](https://rubyllm.com/configuration-providers/) ## A complete AI framework for Ruby More than a client for model APIs. RubyLLM gives your application the conventions, the runtime, and every piece in between, designed to work together. Everything below ships in RubyLLM 2.1. ### Conversations * **Chat:** Conversational AI with `RubyLLM.chat` * **Streaming:** Real-time responses with blocks * **Attachments:** Ask about images, videos, audio, PDFs, and other documents with `with:` * **Structured output:** Define a Ruby schema and read the result with `response.parsed` * **Extended thinking:** Control, view, and persist model deliberation * **Citations:** Normalized source citations from documents, search, and grounding * **Promp
